calibration_anchor.note: Drew ground truth 2026-07-25: 36% of total weekly usage, 30% of fable allowance, against internal-$ ledger sums since the 2026-07-24T00:00Z weekly reset. Limits are DERIVED from this anchor (per-axis): weekly = internal_total/drew_total_pct; fable_allowance = internal_fable/drew_fable_pct. Re-anchor whenever Drew reports fresh percentages.

_semantics: The governor (mr-situation) reads the plan's real utilisation from mr-rate-limit-telemetry.jsonl and grades it with soft_pause_frac / hard_stop_frac; the dollar figures here decide only for an axis with no reading in force (bundle budget.source = calibration), and scale effective_usd for the per-launch check. On the calibration: soft/hard fracs apply to weekly_limit_usd; fable_ok = fable_spend < fable_guard_frac * fable_allowance_usd (the allowance is its own axis, not a fraction of weekly).
_telemetry_note: telemetry_fresh_s: how long a reading is acted on as read (three hourly ticks; a decision session can hold the tick lock for 90 minutes). telemetry_window_models: plan windows that cover one model although their name does not carry it; seven_day_overage_included is reported only to Fable sessions and is the window the CLI's 'You've reached your Fable limit' rejection names (fixtures/run-cost/rate-limit-rejected.stream). A window whose name carries a model covers that model; any other covers every model.

fable._note: ESTIMATE 1.5x opus (overcount = earlier kill = safe); CALIBRATE from first fable run: ledger total vs mr-cost-watch price

_launch_est_note: What one run of a tier is expected to cost (about p90 of ledger runs 2026-10..11: hard p90 $78, routine p90 $34). mr-situation uses it for live runs' remaining exposure and the per-launch check: budget.launchable_tiers[t] = state NORMAL and projected_usd + launch_est_usd[t] <= hard_stop_frac x weekly_limit_usd. slice_caps_usd stays the cost-watch alert line, not a launch check.
_model_fallback_note: Operator rule 2026-11-14: the ONLY downgrade. A session the plan refuses on a model's OWN limit (a one-model credit stop, e.g. 'You've reached your Fable limit') while the shared windows are not at HARD-STOP continues on the mapped model, same tier and effort: mr-launch.sh continues the refused session at once, and mr-interrupted resumes a slice such a stop interrupted on the mapped model until that stop's reset (after it, on its own model again). New launches still go to their own model first (mr-spawn never holds a model with a fallback on its own window, at any reading); nothing is downgraded ahead of a refusal, so a reset or a mid-window credit restore costs nothing. Remove a key to turn its fallback off.
_costwatch_note: enforce=false => MONITOR mode (warn flag + logs only; no stop/kill). Arm after live-run verification that subagent usage streams in real time (adversarial-review blocking condition F3): compare mr-cost-watch price <log> timeline vs ledger on one completed run.
_stream_factor_note: Factor is for REPORTING/calibration only — enforcement thresholds use the RAW sum (overcount fires early = safe direction; adversarial review verdict). Measured: raw overcounts ~25% (312/893 dup events, fixture battle-0hp); ledger/raw=0.80. Recalibrate from (ledger, COSTWATCH final-raw) pairs.
_calibration_note: Since 2026-11-26 weekly_limit_usd (and fable_allowance_usd, scaled by the same ratio) come from `calibration_fit`: the median of ledger dollars per unit of the plan's own seven_day utilisation rise over the last 9 qualifying closed windows, MERGED/LAUNCH rows excluded (mr-budget-calibrate). calibration_anchor is the July operator reading, kept as history. The tick re-checks the fit weekly (`--check`) and asks the operator when it drifts by more than 20%; it never rewrites this file.

calibration_fit.method: median of within-window ledger $ / utilisation rise, closed seven_day windows with rise >= 0.20, last 9, MERGED/LAUNCH rows excluded (mr-budget-calibrate)
